nodes.label: Spec 0002: One planning path: a scope row first, then a spec
Decision: a new capability is planned as a scope row and designed in a spec before code; docs/plans and new ADRs are retired in a single change
nodes.rationale: Practice already chose: six shared rows, both app workspaces and spec 0001 were written on this path, and no plan was ever written under docs/plans. Moving the rules to match costs a handful of sentence edits, while moving practice to match the rules would mean hand writing files no command keeps current. A spec carries everything an ADR does plus the design, so keeping both adds a sorting step with no reader who needs the difference.

nodes.label: Premise: the change removes more than it adds (one folder goes, one record kind stops growing, no new rule file)
nodes.rationale: The easy fix for two planning paths is a third document that explains both, which leaves three doors.

nodes.label: Four homes for planning and decision records: docs/plans, docs/decisions, docs/scope, docs/specs
Retired planning guide docs/plans/README.md (asked for a PRD and a plan per capability; no plan was ever written)
Force: practice and rules disagree (planning went into the scope and a spec while the rules pointed to docs/plans)
Force: agents act on what AGENTS.md links (and would write a PRD in a folder nobody reads)
Force: an ADR and a spec hold the same content (context, options, a decision, consequences)
Force: deferred work is listed twice, and two lists drift
Force: the validator requires docs/plans/README.md and does not know the scope index exists
Force: one maintainer, so the path has to be short enough to hold in the head
Force: /scope rewrites the scope files, so wording there can change without a review of the rule
Option 1 (chosen): scope row first, then a spec, in one change
nodes.rationale: Matches what already happens, leaves one record kind going forward, removes a folder and a list and adds no rule file. Costs: /scope and /architect live outside the repository, and four links and one validator entry change at once.

nodes.label: Option 2 (rejected): the plans folder is the path
nodes.rationale: Nothing writes to docs/plans, so every plan would be written by hand while the scope and specs are kept by commands, and a plan and a spec would describe the same capability twice.

nodes.label: Option 3 (rejected): keep every home, with a written split
nodes.rationale: Four borders to explain and keep in step for one maintainer and one greeting, and every new document would start with the question of which folder it belongs in.

nodes.label: Delete the guide, do not leave a pointer
nodes.rationale: A pointer file is still a second door, and the validator would keep requiring it.

nodes.label: The planning rule lives in docs/rules/development-rules.md
nodes.rationale: That file already owns the sentence about plans and ADRs. The scope index was the runner up and lost because /scope rewrites it.

nodes.label: Files first, commands noted
nodes.rationale: The rule names folders and what each file holds, then says which commands usually write them, so a contributor without those commands can still follow the path.

nodes.label: Triggers stay with their owners
nodes.rationale: The service rules, dependency rules and quality checks each keep their own trigger sentence and only the word for the record changes. Gathering them into one list would create the second copy that spec 0001 forbids.

nodes.label: Decide first, always: a spec before code reaches main
nodes.rationale: Building first on an assumed decision is not used here.

nodes.label: The scope is the brief (no PRD file)
nodes.rationale: The user outcome and the done when line in a row are the product brief, so no PRD file exists to drift from it.

nodes.label: ADR 0001 is not reworded
nodes.rationale: An accepted record keeps its text. Only its status line changes, and only if a later spec replaces it.

nodes.label: Results go where they already live: progress in the scope row, what ran in docs/quality/verification.md
No backfill of specs for shipped capabilities
nodes.rationale: Shipped capabilities get a spec only when a later change to them is a new capability or hits a trigger.

nodes.label: Recommendation: relabel the ownership matrix row to 'Architecture, decision records, scope and agent workflow'
nodes.rationale: Leaving the old label would keep the one word (ADRs) that sends a reader looking for ADR files.

nodes.label: Recommendation: spec 0001 is brought in step in the same change
nodes.rationale: Its own premise note says a rule file changes first and the matching row follows in the same change. Waiting would leave an accepted spec quoting a rule that no longer exists.

nodes.label: Recommendation: name no folder before it has a file
nodes.rationale: docs/reviews/ and similar are added to the repository structure when their first file lands, in line with real caller first.

nodes.label: Canonical pattern: a scope row (the brief), a spec before code, one slice through its real caller, progress in the scope row and results in the verification record
Spec triggers for a smaller change stay in their owner files (service rules, dependency rules, architecture compliance, FFI conventions, ADR 0001 Revisit when)
Record keeping: specs live in docs/specs/<workspace>/NNNN-kebab-title.md, a spec is the record the rules ask for, accepted records are superseded and not reworded, the maintainer approves
Spec status lifecycle: /architect writes Proposed, /develop moves it to In Progress and then Accepted as the scope row moves
Practices the standard replaces (a PRD or plan under docs/plans, a new ADR file, a second deferred list, code before its spec, 'plan' and 'ADR' as record names)
Enforcement: REQUIRED_DOCS drops plans/README and adds scope/index; whether a row and a spec exist and came first rests on review
Rollout: one change in fifteen ordered steps (rules, AGENTS.md, architecture docs, README, validator, delete docs/plans, scope files, spec 0001, knowledge graph)
nodes.rationale: The steps are ordered so the checks never point at a missing file.

nodes.label: Rollout step 15: regenerate the knowledge graph (/graphify) and commit graphify-out in the same change
nodes.rationale: The graph still describes the old guide and the ADR rule, and agents read it first.

nodes.label: Completion checks: validator and test.sh pass, docs/plans is gone, no rule asks for an ADR, plan or PRD, one deferred list, every relative link resolves, the graph has no docs/plans node
Exceptions: ADR 0001 stays as written and required, specs may name docs/plans and ADRs as history, a change that hits no trigger needs neither a row nor a spec, shipped capabilities need no spec yet
Positive: one step from AGENTS.md to the scope index, one record kind, one deferred list, the validator guards the landing page in use, one folder fewer
Tradeoff: /scope and /architect are not part of the repository; a contributor without them writes both files by hand
Tradeoff: the scope landing page can change shape without a rule change; the validator checks only that it exists and is not empty
Tradeoff: whether a capability has a row and a spec, and whether the spec came first, rests on review by one person (and /develop can still offer to build first)
Tradeoff: docs/decisions stays as a folder with one file that will never get a sibling; a reader may look for ADR 0002
Tradeoff: outside links to docs/plans/README.md stop working
Neutral: the first feature needing a record, typed error or async call across the bridge now produces a spec where spec 0001 expected an ADR
Follow-up: nothing checks that files linked from docs/scope/index.md exist (a link check in check-architecture.py)
Follow-up: record where /scope and /architect come from when a second contributor joins
Follow-up: check the Deferred paragraph after each /scope run (it could bring back 'product brief' wording or a second deferred list)
Follow-up: the knowledge graph under graphify-out is a derived copy of the rules and nothing checks that it is current
Follow-up: add docs/reviews/ to repository-structure.md when its first file lands
Follow-up: if checks are ever required before main, consider catching a new capability without a spec there

hyperedges.label: One planning path: a scope row first, then a spec before code, named by the agent instructions, the development rules and the repository structure
Spec triggers kept in their owner files: when a smaller change needs a spec
